scenes.headline: WHY DOES THE OCEAN MOVE?
scenes.caption: Ocean currents are enormous rivers of moving seawater. Some flow at the surface. Others travel deep below.
scenes.narration: Ocean currents are enormous rivers of moving seawater. Some flow at the surface. Others travel deep below.

scenes.headline: WINDS DRIVE THE SURFACE
scenes.caption: Wind pushes surface currents, while Earth's rotation helps curve their paths around the planet.
scenes.narration: Wind pushes surface currents, while Earth's rotation helps curve their paths around the planet.

scenes.headline: COLD WATER SINKS
scenes.caption: In colder regions, seawater can become denser and sink toward the deep ocean.
scenes.narration: In colder regions, seawater can become denser and sink toward the deep ocean.

scenes.headline: THE DEEP OCEAN CIRCULATES
scenes.caption: Temperature and salinity differences help power deep circulation across entire ocean basins.
scenes.narration: Temperature and salinity differences help power deep circulation across entire ocean basins.

scenes.headline: CURRENTS SHAPE CLIMATE
scenes.caption: Ocean currents transport heat, oxygen, and nutrients. They shape marine ecosystems and influence regional climates.
scenes.narration: Ocean currents transport heat, oxygen, and nutrients. They shape marine ecosystems and influence regional climates.

scenes.headline: A PLANET IN MOTION
scenes.caption: Scientists measure these moving waters to understand our changing planet and the ocean's vital role.
scenes.narration: Scientists measure these moving waters to understand our changing planet and the ocean's vital role.
